title: ChatGPT v.s. Media Bias: A Comparative Study of GPT-3.5 and Fine-tuned Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating GPT-3.5's zero-shot classification performance using specific prompts to detect loaded or emotionally charged language, comparing its Micro and Macro F1-scores against fine-tuned models (BART, ConvBERT, GPT-2) on a subset of the Media Bias Identification Benchmark (MBIB).

Evaluating GPT-3.5's zero-shot classification performance using specific prompts to detect subjective tone and underlying prejudices, comparing its Micro and Macro F1-scores against fine-tuned models on a subset of the MBIB dataset.

Evaluating GPT-3.5's zero-shot classification performance using specific prompts to identify language promoting hatred or discrimination towards specific groups, comparing its Micro and Macro F1-scores against fine-tuned models on a subset of the MBIB dataset.

Evaluating GPT-3.5's zero-shot classification performance using specific prompts to identify emotionally charged language, logical fallacies, and false assertions, comparing its Micro and Macro F1-scores against fine-tuned models on a subset of the MBIB dataset.

Evaluating GPT-3.5's zero-shot classification performance using specific prompts to detect language perpetuating stereotypes or negative perceptions of racial groups, comparing its Micro and Macro F1-scores against fine-tuned models on a subset of the MBIB dataset.

Evaluating GPT-3.5's zero-shot classification performance using specific prompts to detect harmful stereotypes, discrimination, or reinforcement of gender roles, comparing its Micro and Macro F1-scores against fine-tuned models on a subset of the MBIB dataset.
